papers.title: Expert Review on the Use of Methylphenidate in Children and Adult With Epilepsy and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a comorbidity affecting 12%-29% of individuals with epilepsy, significantly impacting learning, psychosocial development, behaviour, and quality of life. Moreover, ADHD and epilepsy share a bidirectional relationship. Although methylphenidate has been proven effective in alleviating ADHD symptoms, its use remains limited in individuals with epilepsy due to outdated concerns-dating back over 20 years-that psychostimulants could increase seizure frequency. This manuscript presents a narrative review of the scientific literature published between January 2000 and May 2026 regarding the use of methylphenidate in patients with epilepsy and ADHD. Based on the available evidence, a panel of paediatric neurologists from five Spanish tertiary hospitals with expertise in epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders reached an expert consensus and developed a series of practical recommendations for the assessment and management of these patients. This expert group issued several recommendations, including the proactive screening of ADHD symptoms in all children and adults with epilepsy from the onset of the condition. Current evidence has not consistently demonstrated an increased seizure risk associated with methylphenidate in patients with epilepsy, although available data remain limited for some epilepsy subgroups. Furthermore, undertreatment of ADHD is associated with poorer patient outcomes. Methylphenidate may be considered in children and adults with epilepsy when clinically indicated, following optimization of epilepsy management, associated comorbidities, and behavioural and psychosocial interventions. Treatment decisions should be individualized, particularly in patients with active epilepsy, drug-resistant epilepsy, recent seizure worsening, or developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. papers.title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Relationship Education Within a Nurse Home Visiting Program to Improve Mental Health and Prevent Substance Use Among First-Time, Low-Income Mothers.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To study home visiting programs augmented with relationship education addressing maternal depression (MD), substance use (SU), and self-harm ideation (SHI). METHODS: We performed a secondary data analysis of a three-wave longitudinal randomized controlled trial of the Nurse-Family Partnership (NFP) program. In Oregon, 238 low-income, first-time pregnant mothers were randomized to a standard or augmented program where trained nurses integrated the Within My Reach curriculum and intimate partner violence screening and referral with the NFP workflow one-on-one at home visits. Nurses maintained good fidelity in the augmented program, tailored training to clients' immediate needs, and were advised not to share with the staff in the standard program. At pregnancy, 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups, research assistants interviewed mothers with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (including an SHI item), Alcohol Use Disorder Identification Test, and Drug Abuse Screening Test. Multilevel models and generalized estimating equations with the wave-intervention interactions were performed for MD, SHI, and SU, adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, education level, and nativity status. RESULTS: Depressive symptoms (25%), SU (36%), and SHI (6%, 7%, 9% across 3 waves) were common. Compared with the standard program, the augmented program indicated a stable romantic relationship with the child's father (66% vs. 50%, p = 0.01) and reduced depressive symptoms at the 1-year follow-up (p = 0.02) but did not reduce depressive symptoms, SHI, or SU over the two years. CONCLUSIONS FOR PRACTICE: The findings can guide pragmatic research identifying mechanisms of change and integrating partner engagement, co-parenting, and targeted approaches to depression, SHI and SU into real-world home visiting services. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT01811719 https//clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT01811719.

papers.title: Expression of progesterone, estrogen, and Ki-67 receptors in vaginal tumors of bitches.
papers.abstract: Vaginal neoplasms predominantly affect elderly and intact females. Given the close relationship of sex hormones with reproductive tract carcinogenesis, this retrospective study of 36 female dogs evaluated, by immunohistochemistry, the expression of estrogen and progesterone receptors and the cell proliferation marker Ki-67 in canine vaginal neoplasms, aiming to correlate them with malignancy and clinical variables. The results demonstrated that malignant neoplasms retained estrogen receptor expression, although immunolabeling of both hormone receptors declined with increasing animal age. Older bitches presented smaller tumor diameters at diagnosis, and significant co-expression between estrogen and progesterone receptors was also observed in tumor tissue. The Ki-67 index showed no correlation with malignancy or survival time. The higher prevalence in older females suggests an oncogenesis driven by the accumulation of estrous cycles and chronic hormone exposure.

papers.title: Awareness, attitudes toward epilepsy, and first-aid knowledge of seizures among rural primary care doctors in Eastern China.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess the awareness of, and attitudes toward epilepsy among young rural primary care doctors from rural clinics in Zhejiang Province, Eastern China. METHODS: Ninety-five young rural primary care doctors working at rural clinics participated in this cross-sectional study in 2025. A custom-built electronic questionnaire, which comprised four sections, including 12 items for general condition data, 10 items for awareness (including first aid), a 16-item scale for attitudes, and 6 items for demographic data, was administered to the rural primary care doctors. Descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Kruskal-Wallis H test, and Spearman's rank correlation analysis were used to analyze the data, which exhibited a non-normal distribution. Multivariable linear regression analyzes were conducted to identify independent predictors for each outcome, using the enter method and reporting β, B with 95% CI, p-values, and R2. RESULTS: The young rural primary care doctors obtained a mean score of 18.20 ± 3.48 (aggregate score: 30) on the awareness of epilepsy section, a mean score of 5.40 ± 1.53 (aggregate score: 7) on the first aid knowledge section, and a mean score of 66.05 ± 7.65 (aggregate score: 80) on the epilepsy attitude section. Educational background (rs = 0.293, p = 0.004), training experience (rs = 0.322, p = 0.001), and epilepsy attitude scores (rs = 0.255, p = 0.013) correlated significantly with mean epilepsy awareness scores. Training experience (rs = 0.222, p = 0.031) correlated significantly with attitudes toward epilepsy. papers.title: A Rotary DNA Mazzocchio Nanostructure.
papers.abstract: DNA nanotechnology offers architectures ranging from compact motifs to scaffolded origami, with trade-offs in structural complexity, addressability, and component economy. Here, we translate Leonardo da Vinci's mazzocchio geometry into a programmable DNA assembly. Twenty distinct DNA strands hierarchically assemble into a toroid comprising 32 repeating octagonal subunits. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, transmission electron microscopy, and atomic force microscopy support formation of the designed architecture while revealing flexibility at intersubunit connections. The toroid was coupled to a triangular DNA origami platform through 12 DNA walkers distributed among three vertices. Sequential toehold-mediated strand displacement altered the attachment topology between the two structures, generating three docking configurations. Gel electrophoresis and ensemble fluorescence measurements produced the expected state-dependent responses, consistent with programmed repositioning. This work expands the design space of dynamic DNA nanotechnology through coupling of a material-efficient toroidal architecture with the spatial addressability of origami, establishing a versatile platform for reconfigurable nanoscale devices.

papers.title: Negotiating Genetic Risk: Tunisian Adolescents' Attitudes Toward Marriage, Reproduction, and Hereditary Blood Disorders.
papers.abstract: Hemoglobinopathies, such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia, pose a significant public health challenge in Tunisia. Effective prevention relies on informed reproductive choices shaped by genetic knowledge, socio-cultural norms, emotional bonds, and religious beliefs. This study explores how Tunisian high school students perceive genetic risk in relation to marriage and reproduction following a contextualized educational session on sickle cell disease. A qualitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 158 final-year science students (aged 17-22, 78% female) in two public schools. Participants responded to three hypothetical scenarios involving sickle cell disease and one open-ended question on abortion. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative responses were thematically coded in NVivo. Students demonstrated basic genetic understanding, though misconceptions about carrier status persisted. Emotional attachment frequently outweighed genetic considerations: 58% (92/158) were open to marrying a partner with homozygous sickle cell disease, and 83% (131/158) to marrying a heterozygous carrier. Attitudes toward abortion were strongly influenced by religious values, with 54% (85/158) disagreeing with a couple's decision not to terminate an affected pregnancy. Consanguinity did not arise spontaneously in responses. These post-exposure, scenario-conditioned findings, collected immediately after an educational session featuring patient narratives, are hypothesis-generating. They highlight the need for genetics education that integrates ethical, emotional, and culturally relevant discussions and underscore the importance of further research on unprompted attitudes.

papers.title: The Stress Localization Function─A Stress-Derived Real-Space Descriptor for Chemical Bonding Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.abstract: Existing quantum-chemical topology descriptors, including the Laplacian of the electron density, the Electron Localization Function (ELF), and the Localized Orbital Locator (LOL), characterize bonding through the density and its low-order derivatives, but they trace the localization of electrons rather than the local balance between the kinetic and potential energy densities and sometimes fail in cases such as heavy atoms, hypervalent centers, and bonds of intermediate character. To address these deficiencies, we introduce the Stress Localization Function (SLF), a real-space bonding descriptor constructed from the quantum-mechanical stress tensor. The trace of the stress tensor is the local virial field, which connects the kinetic and potential energy at each point in space. The SLF is obtained by taking its magnitude, comparing it to the value for a uniform electron gas of the same local density, and mapping the result onto a bounded scale, in analogy to the ELF or LOL. Applied to atoms across the periodic table, the SLF resolves the complete electronic shell structure, including the outermost shells of heavy atoms that the Laplacian fails to recover and that stress-based indicators have not resolved with any single choice of parameter. For the 4d elements, the SLF recovers the full complement of shells with no adjustable parameter. It registers the number of occupied shells rather than the nominal period, as shown by palladium's anomalous 4d105s0 configuration. The core value is essentially universal (≈0.578), transferable from free atoms to bonded environments. Across a benchmark set of single, double, and triple bonds, the SLF decreases monotonically with bond order while simultaneously tracking bond polarity through the electronegativity of the bonding partner, separating two distinct chemical effects within a single scalar field. The descriptor further characterizes nonprototypical bonding, including three-center bonds, as in the textbook example of H3+

papers.title: Heterogeneous Dyadic Quality of Life Profiles in Heart Failure Patient‒Caregiver Dyads: A Latent Profile Analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure affects both patients and their caregivers, yet patterns of quality of life (QoL) alignment or mismatch within patient-caregiver dyads remain insufficiently understood. OBJECTIVE: To identify heterogeneity of dyadic QoL profiles in heart failure patient‒caregiver dyads through latent profile analysis and to examine factors associated with profile membership. METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study including 201 heart failure patient-caregiver dyads from four tertiary hospitals in Beijing, China, between September 2023 and August 2024. QoL, symptom burden, caregiver burden, dyadic relationship quality, and family functioning were assessed. Latent profile analysis was performed using Mplus 8.3 and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with profile membership. RESULTS: Three profiles were identified: (1) the low dyadic QoL profile (39.8%), with poor QoL in both members; (2) the incongruent dyadic QoL profile (27.4%), characterized by lower patient QoL and relatively higher caregiver QoL; and (3) the high dyadic QoL profile (32.8%) in both members. With the high dyadic QoL profile as the reference category, greater caregiver burden (OR=1.32, 95% CI=1.14‒1.53) and poorer caregiver-reported relationship quality (OR=1.15, 95% CI=1.01‒1.30) were associated with greater odds of membership in the low dyadic QoL profile. Higher patient symptom burden was associated with greater odds of the low and incongruent profiles than the high profile (both OR=1.04, 95% CI=1.02‒1.06). Dyads with non-spousal caregivers had higher odds of membership in the incongruent profile than in the high dyadic QoL profile (OR=11.49, 95% CI=1.78‒74.23). CONCLUSION: Three distinct dyadic QoL profiles were identified among heart failure patient‒caregiver dyads. papers.title: Nature, nurture, and 5-HT4R: Familial predisposition, not parental bonding, is associated with brain 5-HT4R in a sex-specific manner.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) aggregates in families. The neostriatum, key to reward and attachment circuits, has the highest density of serotonin 4 receptors (5-HT4R). Striatal 5-HT4R is low in MDD and linked to familial depression risk. Poor parental bonding increases depression risk, yet whether nature and nurture converge on 5-HT4R is unknown. We investigated whether parental bonding quality is associated with adult neostriatal 5-HT4R levels and could replicate prior findings on familial predisposition. METHODS: Familial predisposition, parental bonding instrument, and positron emission tomography data with [11C]SB207145 were available from 70 unmedicated MDD patients and 95 healthy controls (64% female; aged 18-57 years). 5-HT4R binding was quantified in the neostriatum and, secondarily, the amygdala, ACC, and neocortex. Linear regression models examined associations among 5-HT4R binding, familial predisposition to depression, and parental bonding, adjusting for sex, age, depression, and tracer mass. Sensitivity analyses were conducted with adjustments for hormonal contraceptives and within the healthy subsample only. RESULTS: Familial predisposition linked to neostriatal 5-HT4R differently by sex (sex interaction, P = 0.037): predisposed females had 6.8% higher binding than non-predisposed females (P = 0.024); males showed no significant difference in association. This was consistent across sensitivity analyses and secondary regions. Parental bonding was not associated with 5-HT4R in any region. CONCLUSION: Familial predisposition to depression is associated with neostriatal 5-HT4R in a sexually dimorphic manner, suggesting that inherited depression risk influences the serotonergic system through sex-specific mechanisms. The absence of parental bonding effects suggests that the impact on the serotonergic system may be subtle or compensated for.

papers.title: Mica-Polyethylenimine Membranes for High-Efficiency pH-Responsive Nanofiltration Enabled by a Strongly Coupled Charge Flip.
papers.abstract: The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica-polyethylenimine membrane using a "coupled charge flip" strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to -36.4 mV) across pH 2-12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from -3.1 to -55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2-12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m-2 h-1 bar-1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.

papers.title: Living hi: GBMSM narratives of pleasure, risk, and everyday hi-fun (chemsex) navigation in Thailand.
papers.abstract: Hi-fun among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) is practiced across Southeast Asia. Yet research remains focused on epidemiological trends and health risks, with limited qualitative work capturing lived experiences, motivations and support needs. These gaps are pronounced in Thailand, where social, legal and cultural structures emphasise control and enforced abstinence over harm reduction and holistic support. This study aims to explore the experiences and perspectives of GBMSM who engage in hi-fun and other types of sexualised drug use, including their strengths and challenges. It seeks to identify the types of support they desire to contribute to the development of harm reduction strategies grounded in the everyday contexts of GBMSM communities in Thailand. This qualitative study drew on five focus group discussions (FGDs) and six in-depth interviews (IDIs) with 30 Thai and non-Thai GBMSM in Bangkok, Khon Kaen and Pattaya. Discussions explored the contexts, experiences, strengths, challenges and support needs related to hi-fun. Thematic analysis was conducted, and findings were reviewed with a community advisory board and partner NGOs. Participants described hi-fun as a distinct world enabling self-expression, pleasure, intimacy and a sense of being valued and accepted beyond what everyday life affords. This world was shaped through equipment preparation, participant screening and unwritten rules promoting trust and safety. Hi-fun offered emotional and social benefits, including connection and belonging. However, participants also reported risks, including mental health challenges, dependence, sexual performance difficulties, violence, non-consensual recording, financial strain and legal consequences. Hi-fun became problematic when individuals lost control, encountered police, were forced into mandatory rehabilitation, experienced health decline or struggled with daily functioning. papers.title: The Importance of Asking "Who": Screening for Intimate Partner Violence Among Patients with Suicidality in the Emergency Department.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Intimate partner violence victimization and perpetration contribute to suicidal ideation and result in about 1800 United States suicides annually. Research indicates that the emergency department population has high rates of suicidal ideation, intimate partner violence, and intimate partner violence-suicidal ideation cooccurrence, making it a potential site for intervention. METHODS: We used a retrospective chart review design to examine 6 months of a university hospital system's electronic medical record to determine if it could be used to identify the number of patients with cooccurring intimate partner violence-suicidal ideation, their role in the intimate partner violence, and to describe intimate partner violence and suicidal ideation screening, disclosure, and treatment. Triage screeners were used to identify patients with positive reports of suicidal ideation and abuse, and emergency department provider notes were reviewed to identify intimate partner violence. RESULTS: Of the 104 patients with positive suicidal ideation and abuse screens at the same ED visit, 27 experienced intimate partner violence (26.0%) and 77 experienced another form of violence ("false positives," 74.0%). Most charts included some details about the intimate partner violence- suicidal ideation presentation and interventions. Suicidal ideation interventions were more varied and utilized than those for intimate partner violence, and no records indicated dual interventions, even when the intimate partner violence and suicidal ideation were described as related. Notably, in nearly half of the false positives, the relationship to the abuse perpetrator was not indicated, suggesting that some intimate partner violence cases may have been missed. DISCUSSION: While this patient population is doubly vulnerable, intimate partner violence and suicidal ideation are often treated in silos, which could increase lethal risk and decrease intervention effectiveness. papers.title: Intimate Partner Homicide - Women are Being Murdered More Than Ever in the United States. What Research Is Needed to Reduce the Carnage?
papers.abstract: This brief opinion outlines the increase in homicide of women by intimate partners, primarily with guns. I make the case that more than half of abused women want to stay with their abusive intimate partners for many complex reasons and that they want to stay safely. They are not being controlled by abusers but rather making rational decisions based on their observations of, and love for the abuser, and concerns for their children. In order for women to stay safely, we need to get more of the abusers into interventions that have been shown to be effective, like Strength At Home and also store guns safely. We need to pay attention to the contemporary brain science that shows us how abusers grow up to use violence against partners and move away from assuming that abusers are motivated by power and control. But we need more and better research to show the efficacy of these approaches.

papers.title: The Reporting-Service Gap in Intimate Partner Violence: Police Reporting, Victim-Service Receipt, and Dual Noncontact in the National Crime Victimization Survey, 1993-2023.
papers.abstract: Research on intimate partner violence (IPV) underreporting often treats police notification as the primary indicator of formal-system reach, leaving less clear whether incidents not reported to police include recorded receipt of help or advice from victim-service agencies. Using incident-level public-use data from the National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS), 1993 to 2023, this study examines the joint distribution of police reporting and receipt of victim-service help or advice among IPV violent victimizations. The analytic sample included 7,672 incidents. A four-category outcome distinguished incidents involving no police report and no recorded victim-service receipt, police reporting only, victim-service receipt only, or both. Dual noncontact was defined at the incident level as no police report and no recorded receipt of victim-service help or advice. Survey-weighted estimates, design-adjusted confidence intervals, reporting-status contrasts, stated reasons for police nonreporting, and a design-based multinomial model described the two measured channels. In 2018 to 2023, 43.0% of IPV violent victimizations involved dual noncontact, 34.3% involved police reporting only, 7.2% involved victim-service receipt only, and 15.5% involved both. Recorded victim-service receipt was more common among police-reported incidents (31.2%, 95% CI [24.9, 38.2]) than among unreported incidents (14.3%, 95% CI [9.9, 20.3]). This reporting-status difference did not vary significantly across the six periods, F(5, 550) = 0.61, p = .693. Among incidents with no police report and no recorded victim-service receipt, the leading stated reasons for police nonreporting were privacy or personal-matter concerns (26.6%), not wanting the offender to get in trouble (24.2%), and fear of reprisal (14.7%). These responses characterize police nonreporting only and do not explain why victim-service receipt was absent. The results provide a long-term descriptive benchmark and support direct evaluation

papers.title: Physical Intimate Partner Violence Across Heterosexual, Gay, and Lesbian Relationships.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) has traditionally been conceptualized as a gendered phenomenon rooted in male perpetration and female victimization. However, evidence of IPV within same-sex relationships raises important questions regarding explanations that emphasize relationship gender composition as a primary determinant of partner violence. This study examined whether physical IPV involvement differed across heterosexual, gay male, and lesbian relationships using relationship records from Wave III of the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health), a nationally representative longitudinal study of adolescents in the United States. The eligible sample included 11,941 sexual relationships; analyses of physical IPV were based on 5,868 relationships with usable IPV data, with adjusted logistic regression models estimated using 5,617 complete cases. Physical IPV was measured using four behaviorally specific indicators of aggression and victimization. Group differences were examined using chi-square tests, analysis of variance, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, race/ethnicity, income, and educational attainment. Physical IPV was reported in 25.98% of heterosexual relationships, 26.42% of gay male relationships, and 26.00% of lesbian relationships. No statistically significant association between relationship type and physical IPV involvement was detected after adjustment for demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Although the observed prevalence estimates were numerically similar across relationship types, the relatively small same-sex subsamples limit precision and preclude ruling out potentially meaningful differences. The absence of a statistically significant association is compatible with theoretical perspectives emphasizing factors that operate across relationship types, although the study does not directly test competing theoretical mechanisms.

papers.title: How to Institutionalize and Individualize Educational Programs to Prevent Violence.
papers.abstract: We need to build broader, comprehensive and well-established curricula incorporating violence prevention along with other life skills, prevention practices, health information, character building and decision-making. We might be able to take advantage of the curricular revolution that is likely to arrive soon. This revolution will be from the greater deployment of artificial intelligence to personalize the learning process. Strategies are needed to overcome the obstacles to the collaborations required to create these comprehensive curricula. Evaluations are needed of these comprehensive approaches.

papers.title: Working alliance in HIV counseling and testing: Team and mobile counseling models.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: HIV Counseling and Testing Centers play an important role in reaching populations at increased risk for HIV infection. Although different counseling modalities are used in these settings, little is known about the relational quality of brief HIV counseling encounters. Working alliance (WA), a core indicator of relationship quality in psychotherapy and health care, has not previously been examined in HIV counseling. This study investigated whether WA can be established during brief HIV counseling sessions and whether it differs across counseling modalities, professional backgrounds, and testing settings. METHODS: A quasi-experimental study was conducted with 253 first-time users of an HIV testing center in Portugal. Participants were allocated to one of three counseling conditions (team counseling, nurse-led counseling, psychologist-led counseling) or to a control condition (information only). Sessions took place in a stand-alone center or a mobile unit. Users and professionals completed the Working Alliance Inventory, and WA scores were analyzed using MANOVA and post-hoc tests. RESULTS: Working alliance was established across all counseling modalities and settings. From the users' perspective, team counseling resulted in higher WA scores, whereas professionals rated WA lower in team sessions than in individual sessions. No significant differences in WA were found between stand-alone and mobile settings or between nurse- and psychologist-led counseling. All counseling conditions also showed significantly higher WA scores than the information-only condition (p < .001). CONCLUSION: Meaningful working alliance can be established during a single HIV counseling session, regardless of setting or professional background. From the user perspective, team-based counseling was associated with higher relational quality, while mobile counseling appeared to support relational quality comparably to stand-alone services.
